explanation: The text stresses that Smith used the invisible-hand metaphor only once, for a narrow point, and that it became famous because twentieth-century economists inflated it to give their own views an intellectual pedigree. So the metaphor's reputation comes from later promotion, not from its role in Smith's work. B wrongly endorses the metaphor as a useful model, and C invents a 'subtle critique' the text never mentions.

About 80% of drawings showed a mammal, compared with roughly 68% for birds and 55% for insects. Mammals appearing more often than either other group supports the idea that children are more aware of mammals. C reverses the graph, and A and B are inaccurate or irrelevant to mammals.

Schmidt never says he disapproves of the wife's opinion; instead he winces, sighs dramatically, and invents an obviously fake appointment. His feelings are communicated through actions rather than stated outright. B fails because the text makes clear there was no forgotten appointment at all, and nothing suggests an earlier disagreement (C) or that he is theatrical only with these people (A).

The hypothesis is that the plants depend on dissolving rock to create growth channels. If the roots carve brand-new openings even when ready-made cracks are available, that shows the plants actively dissolve rock rather than just using existing gaps. D would actually weaken the phosphorus part of the hypothesis, and A and B say nothing about whether the plants rely on dissolving rock.

Around 2,000 years ago Siberian dogs suddenly show Near Eastern ancestry and Near Eastern artifacts appear, yet the Siberian people didn't travel far. The logical conclusion is that dogs and goods were being brought into Siberia from the Near East. B contradicts the evidence that Siberians didn't travel extensively, and C and D describe exchanges the text gives no evidence for.

Gayah claims that banning left turns at busy intersections improves traffic flow and cuts travel times. Delivery drivers reaching more addresses each day after such a ban shows faster overall travel. D shows the opposite effect, and A and B are about left-turn signals rather than eliminating left turns.

The claim is that Dai's early pieces reflect dances of local communities she visited. A quotation saying Yao Drum was inspired by a ceremonial dance Dai saw while doing field research among the Yao people directly supports this. The other choices describe the dance's sound, structure, or physicality without linking it to a local community.

In C the Rock declares that it is 'set to encounter' the Sea and 'to limit thy power,' which is exactly the intention to confront and restrain the sea. A shows the Rock being attacked but not its intention, and B and D are spoken by the Sea.

Fynbos roots spread widely to absorb soil nutrients, and forest seedlings grew five times faster when kept away from those roots. This suggests the fynbos roots take up so many nutrients that forest plants can't thrive there, keeping the forest from spreading. There's no evidence the roots physically damage other roots (A) or form a physical wall (B).

The recommendation is to use only small amounts of SSA to avoid losing strength. A shows that 10% SSA was about as strong as or stronger than the control on both days, while 20% and 40% SSA were weaker, which is exactly the pattern that supports using small proportions. C is inaccurate because the 10% mixture's strength did not decrease, and B and D don't compare small and large proportions against the control.

The example needs to show evaluations varying widely by occupation. C contrasts 82% 'likely' for tour guides with only 16% for surgeons, a huge difference across occupations. A describes only one occupation, B highlights a similarity, and D gives a single figure with no comparison.

D says Patty used all the diplomacy she had, dwelling 'touchingly' on the friends' long friendship and sorrow at separation, which shows her working hard to persuade Mrs. Trent. A focuses on Mrs. Trent, and B and C describe moments after or apart from the persuasion attempt.

The flower flourishes only if dew and rain nourish it, and the mind flourishes only if fed by the 'sweet dew' of the spirit; without it, both languish. So the mind, like the flower, needs proper nourishment to thrive. D is tempting, but the poem says the mind withers in hard conditions rather than persevering.

Rio Grande Valley turkeys share genetic markers with Mesa Verde turkeys only after 1280, right when the Ancestral Puebloans abandoned their villages. The best explanation is that some of them moved to the Rio Grande Valley and brought their turkey-farming practices along. C and D make claims about other peoples' farming that the text doesn't support.

Among resolution makers, 58% of those 50-64 make relationship resolutions versus 53% of those 30-49, and 56% make finance resolutions versus 63%. That matches A exactly. B is wrong because 79% (18-29) is not more than 80% (30-49), and C and D draw conclusions the table can't support.

The text reports van Berlo et al.'s finding that advergames may not help players recall brand information, then uses Lang's limited capacity model to explain why: players spend their mental resources on game mechanics. A captures this finding-plus-explanation structure. B wrongly says Lang drew the conclusion about advergames, and C and D add claims about purchasing or success that the text doesn't make.

The speaker admires Dunbar for having 'read the hearts and souls of men' and the 'language of the flowers,' with even the brook answering his call. This praises his deep insight into both people and nature. B takes 'read' too literally, and nothing describes a writing process (C) or a shared afternoon (D).

The conclusion is that irrigation increases but the size of the increase depends heavily on how concentrated precipitation already is. B shows irrigation rising only 0.4% and 0.9% where precipitation is already somewhat concentrated but 9.0% and 7.9% where it is evenly distributed. D misstates the data as a decline and mislabels the numbers, and A and C focus on aquifer input or don't compare the two baselines for irrigation.

Every sentence is about the runestone discovered in Norway: what it might contain, when it was carved, and why it matters. Zilmer is mentioned only as someone commenting on the stone, so D is too narrow, and the text says nothing about battles or a new dating method.

The study found that spike waves, which form when opposing traveling waves meet, can grow taller than the height limit that steepness puts on traveling waves. D states this main point. B is wrong because spike waves exceed the limit due to factors other than steepness, and A wrongly applies jet stability and cavity shape to traveling waves.

The team tested torches, lamps, and fireplaces and learned that each likely had a specific use, such as torches being better for walking. D sums this up. A and B make claims about fireplaces being essential or lamps being used more often that the text doesn't support, and nothing suggests the team was reluctant to draw conclusions (C).

Saturated color is normally an 'honest signal' because it reflects a carotenoid-rich, healthy diet. If tanagers can fake deep saturation with feather microstructures without eating many carotenoids, their color may falsely advertise fitness. A misses that the signal would no longer be honest, and B and C aren't supported by the findings.

The text directly states that newer pits carved on top of older pits led Waweru to think the game was played at the site for a long time. B is why she thought the pits were game boards, not why she thought play lasted a long time.

The conclusion links more competition to more toxin production and less growth. B shows that high-density tadpoles had much higher toxin concentrations (374 vs. 230 and 171 ng/mg) but lower body mass than those in low and medium density, capturing both parts. A covers only body mass, and D focuses on the number of distinct toxins, which barely changed.

The hypothesis was that reflecting on lessons learned from mistakes increases humility. The 'mistake with learning' group scored highest (about 3.1), above both the 'without learning' and control groups. A and D don't compare the groups, and B misreads the graph since the control scored higher than one experimental group.

About 100% of Tanzania's people (around 61 million) speak Swahili, but the text says only up to 15 million people worldwide speak it as a first language. So most Tanzanians must speak Swahili as a second or later language, supporting the claim. B misreads the table, and C and D don't connect speakers to the first-language total.

The text states that surfactants released from microplastics have a much stronger wave-reducing effect than the microplastic particles. The other choices describe properties or uses of surfactants that the text never mentions.

MFC power is limited because electrons must pass through a chain of inefficient redox reactions. Adding highly conductive silver more than doubled power density, so the logical hypothesis is that the silver lets electrons skip those reactions and move straight to the electrode. C introduces bacterial metabolism, which has nothing to do with silver's conductivity, and D ignores the silver entirely.

The claim is that hip-hop pedagogy raises student interest and engagement. High enrollment and attendance in hip-hop courses is direct evidence of student interest and engagement. C is about teachers' enjoyment, not students, and A and B don't support the claim.

The researchers asked whether adaptive radiation that diversified Tetragnatha web designs also changed their silk, and they found significant differences in silk properties between species. B states this. A and D contradict that finding, and C claims a causal link between silk and web design that the study didn't test.

The hypothesis compares wider-headed and narrower-headed fish. C shows the wide-headed bristlemouth hitting obstructions more often than the narrow-headed smooth-hound, which directly supports it. A has no comparison, B compares individuals of one species, and D shows no difference.

Even when disagreeing summaries contained clear signs of attentive listening, participants still rated those listeners as less skilled. This implies participants overlooked the evidence of attentiveness when faced with disagreement. D contradicts the finding that ratings didn't depend on the other traits, and A brings in personal investment, which the text never measures.

Tortoises are solitary and get no parental care, yet their hatchlings still preferred a face-like image. So an innate attraction to faces can't be assumed to exist only because of social life or parental care. C contradicts the idea that the preference is innate, and the study didn't involve adult tortoises (D).
The red maple is native to North America and reaches only 60 feet, meeting both requirements. Silver and sugar maples grow taller than 60 feet, and the Norway maple is not native.

In C the narrator says she's getting fond of the big room but hates the 'horrid' wallpaper, which shows both positive and negative feelings about her surroundings. A and D are entirely negative, and B is a neutral observation.

Ordinary aerogels are brittle and eventually fracture from repeated heating. The new aerogel contracts when heated and fully recovers from heavy compression, so it should be less prone to the weakness that breaks other aerogels down. A gives a cause the text never mentions, and B and C contradict or go beyond the evidence.

Hooked tools are harder to obtain and work better, and crows carefully hold or store them but not basic sticks. That behavior suggests the crows value hooked tools more. Nothing in the text mentions how easy the tools are to hold (B) or sharing (C).

In 2010 computer services had about 6,000 jobs, the same as engineering services; in 2019 it had about 5,000, the same as technical consulting. A is half right but computer services (5,000) did not match engineering (6,000) in 2019, and C and D misread the bars.

To show the nitrogen fertilizer increases yield, you need to compare it with the control. In 2017, 2018, and 2019 the nitrogen bars are all higher than the control bars. A is false for 2019 and makes no comparison, and D tracks only one group over time.

C calls Lady Chiltern someone who doesn't know weakness and stands apart as good women do (very virtuous) but also 'pitiless,' 'cold and stern and without mercy' (unforgiving). A shows only her high principles, and B and D don't address either trait clearly.

The text explains that Cassini detected an odd wobble in Mimas's rotation and that Rhoden's team proposed a hidden ocean could cause it. D sums this up. A overstates the findings (nothing was confirmed for several moons), B contradicts the text, and C misdescribes the model, which was used to study Mimas's wobble.

The example must show species with more fish caught in winter than in the other seasons. The silver-biddy (about 35 in winter vs. 17 and 10) and milkfish (about 12 vs. 7 and 0) both fit. B, C, and D compare species within a season instead of showing a winter peak, and C even names a fish incorrectly.

The claim is that Kelly's decorative buttons were inspired by what he saw the women in his family do when he was a child. C shows his grandmother adding mismatched buttons to clothes during his childhood, which links directly to his button style. D mentions family women but is about sewing and drawing in general, not buttons.

Mary is absorbed in the work, grows more pleased every hour instead of tiring, and finds it like a fascinating game. So she finds caring for the garden deeply satisfying. B contradicts the text, and C misreads 'like a fascinating sort of play' as a plan to make a play space.

The claim is that Coleman deliberately defied social norms through how she presented herself. D shows that female pilots were expected to wear dresses or skirts, but Coleman wore pants and leather jackets. B is about her relationship with staff, not social norms, and A and C don't show any defiance.

The impact theory needs a crater from the start of the Younger Dryas, but Kjær's team doesn't know how old the Greenland crater is. Without a date, they can't link that crater to the start of the cooling period. B, C, and D raise issues about crater size, other causes, or the period's start date that the text never discusses.
Sierra Negra's deformation rate is about 2.9 cm per month, and the only volcano with a higher rate is Pacaya at about 3.3. Alcedo, Fernandina, and Maule all have lower rates than Sierra Negra.

The completion must show differing valuations and that prompting people to consider value raises prices. The students (study 2) chose higher prices than the online group, and in both studies 'pay what you think it's worth' produced the highest prices. A is wrong because students also chose more under 'pay what you can,' B is wrong about the online group in every condition and mentions actual ticket cost (not shown), and D describes individual variation the graph doesn't show.

The journalist claims that collaboration is hard for artists used to controlling their own work. A describes a collective that fell apart because members had trouble sharing credit and responsibility. C says the collective supports individual expression, which works against the claim, and B and D describe arrangements without showing any difficulty.

Allen says the strongest opinions consider and rebut objections. Discussing philosophers who disagree with the judge would surface such objections, so it could make judges' arguments stronger. The other choices bring in readability, avoiding philosophy, or matching popular views, none of which follows from the text.

The text describes shimmering and ends with the researchers' hypothesis that it is a specialized defense against hornets, since it doesn't occur with larger predators. B states this. The text doesn't say hornets are the main predator (C) or that other species shimmer (D).

The explanation is that Mexican art objects reached Missouri through long-distance trade, inspiring a local artist. Finding an ancient Mexican art object at a Mississippian-period site near where the gorget was found shows such objects really did travel there. A and B are about dating and jaguar range rather than trade, and D concerns present-day art.

The text says Johnson still learned what others thought of her plays, and at her gatherings attendees read and discussed each other's work, including hers. So the gatherings gave her a chance to get feedback. A is wrong because these were informal get-togethers, not professional productions.

The text says the counts are bare minimums, so the true totals could be higher. C fits by suggesting St. Cyr acted in far more than 66 films and Carewe directed more than 58. D suggests lower numbers for one of Young Deer's roles, which goes against the idea of minimums, and B conflicts with Carewe's years active.

EBF repels mosquitoes by activating just Or31, a receptor found in every disease-carrying mosquito species. So the most useful next step would be finding molecules like EBF that also target Or31. B, C, and D focus on extraction, receptor locations, or activating many receptors, which miss the point of the Or31 discovery.

Prospero is surprised that Miranda remembers the women who cared for her and says that if she remembers anything from before the island, she may also remember how she arrived. That's the point in C. Nothing suggests her memories are melancholy (A) or a daydream (D), and Prospero actually confirms the memory is real.

Low levels of ALAN didn't affect spawning or fertilization but completely stopped eggs from hatching. So if clownfish settled in places regularly exposed to ALAN (which larvae, drawn to light, might do), their reproduction would be threatened. A and D contradict the reported findings, and C compares to other species that weren't studied.

The claim is that Chambi captured diverse parts of Peruvian society with dignity and authenticity, giving his work ethnographic value. A shows he photographed both wealthy Peruvians and carefully documented Indigenous Andean peoples, sites, and customs. B is about technical skill, C about fame, and D doesn't show anything about Chambi's own approach.

For the before, after, and overall ratings, the velocity correlations (-0.9357, -0.9518, -0.8587) are all farther from 0 than the density correlations (0.8592, 0.7308, 0.7447). That directly shows velocity correlations are stronger. C is true but describes direction, not strength, and A and B compare the wrong pairs.

Wastewater raises delta 15-N values, so influxes that happen only some of the time would make values rise and fall. In Akumal Bay (3.3, 2.0, 6.3) and Tulum (5.9, 2.3, 5.5) the values fluctuated a lot from October 2016 to October 2017. C stresses stability, which works against the idea, and A is inaccurate because Akumal Bay's February 2017 value was not lower than Xahuayxol's.

Washington's bar sits at about 680, which is between 600 and 800. B is wrong because New York had about 1,060 farms, C is wrong because Iowa had only about 730, and D is wrong because Pennsylvania had about 800, not more than 1,200.

Silicon captures red light and perovskite captures blue light. Each alone is only about as efficient as silicon, but together they convert 29.5% or more, so the combined cells must work better by using more of the spectrum. B contradicts the statement that perovskite-only cells are no more efficient than silicon ones.

The ring-counting method depends on being able to see the rings. If many olive trees have rings that are hard to see, the method often can't be used on them, which supports the researcher's claim. The other details are about age, growing conditions, or climate, not about counting rings.
The white-tailed deer has the tallest bar, at about 2.7 million metric tons, more than the wild boar (about 1.9), the elephant (about 1.3), and the kangaroo (about 0.6).

Adults, eggs, and hatchlings were all found at the site, but no juveniles, and the site is used only for reproduction. That suggests the octopuses leave after hatching and before reaching the juvenile, in-between stage. B, C, and D make claims about population stability, egg size, or feeding that the text doesn't address.

Wood exposed to air and water rots quickly unless sediment shields it from oxygen. Since much of the wooden hull survived since the 1500s, it was most likely protected by a layer of sediment. The other choices aren't connected to how the wood was preserved.

To show paywalls help larger papers more, you need to compare a large paper with a small one. C contrasts The New York Times (large, +20%) with the Denver Post (small, -1%). A and B compare only large papers, and D looks at a single small paper and misdescribes -1% as the smallest change.

Red ocher gets its color from iron, while plant pigments are high in carbon. Pigment on some beads had no iron and lots of carbon, so it was likely plant-based rather than ocher. A, C, and D add claims about age, brightness, or ocher's availability that the test can't show.

The program's goal is to restore condors to the wild. The wild population grew from about 230 in 2014 to about 330 in 2020 and stayed above the captive population, which shows success. A is inaccurate since the captive numbers stayed fairly flat, and B and C don't show the program working.

Melanosomes have different shapes depending on the color they produce, and the scientists found them in a fossil feather. So they could use the melanosomes' shapes to figure out the bird's colors. D fails because the method needs melanosomes to be present.
The table lists the Los Coyotes Band's area as 39.21 square miles, which is under 50 square miles and fits the example. The other numbers belong to different tribal nations.

To show longer leave may not help more, the short-leave group should do as well as or better than the long-leave group after leave. On both the second and third tests, the 2-4 days group (about 575 and 510) outscored the 1-5 weeks group (about 520 and 480). B describes scores before leave, and D compares to the no-leave group rather than to longer leave.

The hypothesis predicts squirrels will have longer torpor bouts and shorter arousals than marmots. Marmots averaged 13.81-day bouts and 21.2-hour arousals, versus 16.77 days and 14.2 hours for squirrels, matching C. A is wrong because marmot arousals lasted hours, not days, and B and D don't compare the two species.

The claim is that Puerto Rican guinea pigs descended from Colombian ones. If ancient Puerto Rican guinea pigs were genetically closer to Peruvian guinea pigs than to Colombian ones, that would point to Peru instead. D would, if anything, be neutral or mildly supportive, and B and C say nothing about ancestry.

The claim requires both displeasure and acknowledgment of merit. D does both: the speaker reads poetry 'with a perfect contempt for it' yet finds 'a place for the genuine' in it. B and C criticize bad poetry without praising poetry, and A defends other kinds of writing.

The researchers counted it as misattribution when participants later said a smartphone-retrieved answer came from memory. But if participants already knew that answer before looking it up, saying it came from memory might be accurate, which would inflate the misattribution rate. Answering D would show whether the evidence really supports the hypothesis. A, B, and C address timing, confidence, or accuracy rather than this flaw.

The viola's sound openings point away from the audience because of how the violist sits. To make a solo heard clearly, the logical fix is for the violist to turn toward the audience. Telling others to play louder (A) would drown out the solo, and B and D don't solve the problem.

The text says Moejoh and her team founded the organization to teach young people how their actions affect the environment and why recycling matters. The art exhibit is only an example of their work, not a goal of promoting artists (A).
Females traveled the least in the cold-dry season (9.28 km per day), and so did males (15.81 km per day). Both the monsoon and hot-dry values are higher for each sex.

The hypothesis says acidic soil (with coffee grounds) is better for choy sum growth. If plants in plain soil grew significantly taller, the neutral soil would seem better, weakening the hypothesis. B, C, and D all show the coffee-ground plants doing better, which supports the hypothesis.
